t: Formed around 933 by uniting Upper and Lower Burgundy, it stretched from Lake Geneva to the Mediterranean.
From 1032 it was the third kingdom of the Holy Roman Empire, beside Germany and Italy.
Real power lay with counts, bishops and the houses of Savoy and Viennois; France gradually absorbed its lands.
dyk: In 972 Muslim raiders from Fraxinetum on the Provençal coast captured Abbot Majolus of Cluny in the Alps; the outrage led to the destruction of their base soon afterwards.
ev: Rudolf II of Upper Burgundy acquires Lower Burgundy from Hugh of Arles
Conrad the Peaceful succeeds under the protection of Otto I
Count William of Provence destroys the Muslim base at Fraxinetum
Rudolf III dies childless and the kingdom passes to Emperor Conrad II
Frederick Barbarossa is crowned king at Arles
The Dauphiné of Viennois passes to the heir of the French throne
Charles IV is crowned at Arles, the kingdom’s last coronation
Charles IV makes the French dauphin imperial vicar of the kingdom for life

f.capital: Arles (coronation city); the kings resided mostly around Lake Geneva and at Vienne
f.predecessor: Kingdom of Upper Burgundy; Kingdom of Lower Burgundy
f.successor: Kingdom of France; County of Savoy; Swiss Confederation
